1) the charge fluctuations in a quantum box weakly coupled to an electron reservoir are described by anisotropic two channel Kondo model and 2) the differential capacitance is a good measure of the Kondo temperature and its scaling with the gate voltage is a clear signature of the Kondo effect.

the differential capacitances of the quantum dot and the point contact exhibit a two-channel Kondo behavior, and that the Kondo temperature of the point contact is enhanced due to the presence of electron correlations in the quantum wire.

we show that the two-channel Kondo effect can be enhanced by the electron correlations in the quantum wire.
we show how the Kondo effect can be used to probe the physics of the quantum box, which is the opposite of what is usually the case, i.e. that one uses the quantum box to probe the Kondo effect.
